remainingEvidence: The downward half needs discrimination rather than construction for authority and has no evidence at all for policy: src/authority/runtime.ts#TenantAuthorityRuntime and src/composition/authority.ts already resolve along the ordered Tenant-to-target path under C13-AUTH-DENY-PRECEDENCE and C13-AUTH-PATH-ORDER, while nothing asserts that declared PolicySet material — enforcement tiers, quotas, retention — resolves along that same path, so a host resolving policy per-Workspace only would satisfy every current test

The composition conjunct is true by construction and unasserted, which is the direction a regression arrives from: src/facets/slot-store.ts#WorkspaceSlotCatalog reads a WorkspaceSlotStore and can only return the queried Workspace's own entries, so an ancestor's install cannot compose into a descendant today because no ancestor-scoped slot store exists. Closure needs the adversarial case — a Facet installed at the Tenant, a slot query at a Workspace beneath it, no entry returned — so the confinement survives the day a Tenant-scoped store is added

The Event conjunct cannot be proved by the matcher and has to be proved at the store that supplies candidate Subscriptions: src/workspaces/policy.ts#eventMatches compares kind, source and accepted trust only, so a Subscription (src/workspaces/subscription.ts#Subscription) whose pattern matches an Event accepted by a sibling or ancestor Actor exactly must still be shown never to receive it, and a mutation widening the candidate set past the accepting Actor must break a cited test

The positive cross-Scope path is untested as a Scope statement: a Tenant reacting to a Workspace Event must be shown to require a declared Subscription whose delivery authority is checked under C13-SUBSCRIPTION-AUTHORITY, and the same reaction must be impossible without that Subscription and its Grant, which is what separates a declared route from inherited visibility

Nothing keeps the two directions from being conflated, so the rule needs two mutations of its own: a Grant that stops at the Scope holding it instead of reaching descendants, and a slot entry or an Event that traverses the chain the way a Grant does, each killing a distinct test — a host doing either would violate this rule while satisfying every atom it cites

remainingEvidence: Principal-independence is enforced today at the durable custody boundary and in the custody lookup: BindingCredentialCustody.fromData admits exactly an (endpoint, secret) fact and refuses any further discriminant, and Binding.hasCredentialCustody decides from the (SecretRef, endpoint) pair with no subject input, so two Principals of one Tenant observe the identical answer. That is the half of the rule a record can carry

The other half needs the seam that does not exist yet. C13-CONFIG-SECRET-CUSTODY's remaining provider work is a concrete credential-isolation adapter; until it exists nothing demonstrates that a live resolution presents the (SecretRef, consumer, endpoint) triple with no Principal component, that a resolution refused for one Principal is refused for every Principal of that Tenant, or that a seam offered a Principal-qualified key fails the attempt rather than degrading to a narrower scope
